final_synthesis_description: All three stakeholders agree that essential expenses must never be compromised for a computer purchase; the family should immediately pursue alternative access routes (school loaner programs, library/lab access, community digital equity initiatives, used devices) while applying a phased approach that first secures household stability, then evaluates the full total cost of educational technology access—including internet, software, and peripherals—before considering any purchase.
remaining_disagreements: Degree of specificity in the phased cost-protective rule (e.g., exact sequencing steps and thresholds)
Whether a strict time-and-harm deadline for pursuing alternatives should be explicitly mandated
Whether total ongoing costs (internet, software, peripherals) must be formally itemized as part of the decision criteria
